newsitem.title: GERMANY: Europa Re ups dividend, expects good 1995 figures.
newsitem.headline: Europa Re ups dividend, expects good 1995 figures.

text.p: German reinsurer Europa Rueckversicherung expects another rise in profits for 1996 despite a weaker market, chief executive Rolf Tolle said on Thursday.
"The market as a whole suffered a drop in prices of some 15 to 20 percent. For our company, the price fall was confined to some seven percent," Tolle said.
With skilful retrocession, this still allowed better results. In addition, investment income did well.
In 1997, reinsurance markets would probably be hit by another decline in prices of 15 percent, he added.

The company, which is active mainly in the broker market, lifted post-tax profits in 1995 from 1.6 million marks to 4.3 million marks on gross premium income that rose six percent from 169.0 million marks to 179.2 million marks.
Net income grew by seven percent from 146.8 million marks to 157.4 million marks in the period. The company increased its dividend from eight percent to 10 percent.
Europa Re is controlled by Cologne Re and thus indirectly by General Re of the U.S.

Cologne Re owns 75 percent of Europe Re, while three insurers own eight percent each -- Provinzial Rheinprovinz, Duesseldorf, Provinzial Westfalen, Muenster and Iron Trades Insurance in the UK. France's MAAF holds one percent.
Europa Re was originally set up in 1947 by a group of German and French insurers. Cologne Re, which took over 100 percent of the company in 1963, closed operations down in 1965.
In 1990, Europa Re was revitalised as a specialised broker market reinsurer and Cologne Re sold minority stakes to others.
"Some 83 percent of our business comes from abroad," said Tolle. Seven of the ten major brokers Europa Re works with are based in London.
"Of our gross premium income, 16 percent comes from the UK market, 18 percent from Lloyd's, 17 percent from Germany and ten percent from Italy," he said.

In 1995, fire and other property remained by far the largest line. Income rose 10.7 percent from 94.3 million marks to 104.4 million marks, followed by marine, which was down 13.7 percent from 35.0 million marks to 30.2 million marks.
Motor insurance fell 19.5 percent from 14.9 million marks to 12.0 million marks.
"We suffered little from major losses in 1995," said Tolle. Hurricane Marylin cost four million marks gross and Hurricane Luis two million marks.
1995 ended with an underwriting profit -- before allocations to fluctuation funds -- of 14.7 million marks, compared with 16.5 million marks the year before.
After allocations to fluctuation funds, the company reported a deficit of 4.8 million marks, a slight improvement on the 4.9 million marks of 1994.
Investment income was up from 12.8 million marks to 14.3 million marks, after costs of investments, a pre-tax profit of 7.1 million marks was shown, up from 4.1 million marks in 1994.
